title: Correlation Scout: Annotated Request Timeline + Span Lens Workbench
creator: Maya Brooks
description:
Goal: Design a compact, annotation-first request timeline (Correlation Scout) that surfaces span-level causes, user-impacting latencies, and quick actions for rollouts and cost investigations. The UI should let engineers and SREs rapidly go from a correlation ID to a prioritized root-cause hypothesis using annotated sparkline lanes, span-lens detail, and inline filters.

Problems we solve: slow investigations (~15-30m) because of scattered traces, lack of clear user-impact signals in spans, and difficulty correlating rollout events or model switchovers to latency/quality regressions.

Key features to design: 1) Correlation header with pinned metadata (corr ID, request type, region, dev tag, model variant) and one-click copy/link. 2) Multi-lane request timeline with compact sparkline per service/span-group (mini-heatmaps for latency, error rate, token-cost). 3) Span Lens panel that opens inline (not a separate page) with details: span name, duration histogram, top 3 inferred root causes, KV cache hit/eviction metadata, and suggested follow-ups (view logs, open PR, run evaluation prompt). 4) Temporal scrubber and playback controls to step through the request timeline and see span lifecycles (including KV cache growth). 5) Correlation filters and saved queries: trace-level filter expressions (e.g., model:llama2quant and batch_size>1) with ability to scope to a customer or rollout. 6) Annotated events rail for cross-referencing rollout and infra events (canary start, model fallback, autoscaler surge). 7) Cost microbreakdown hovercards showing estimated token cost per span and per service.

Design constraints and non-goals: keep initial version non-invasive to existing Console layouts; avoid changing core data model or adding heavy backend metrics beyond what the runtime already emits. Non-goal: full request replay or deterministic step-by-step state reconstruction (we do a best-effort playback using available spans and events).

Acceptance criteria: 1) Prototype supports drilling from correlation header to Span Lens in <=2 clicks. 2) Annotated timeline allows filtering to a subset of spans and highlights the top three latency contributors visually. 3) Cost hovercards show estimated token cost within ±20% for sampled traces. 4) Accessibility: keyboard nav to scrubber and open/close lens; color choices pass AA contrast. 5) Performance: initial render of a 200-span trace should be <400ms on a mid-range laptop.

Prototypes and artifacts: Figma prototype: https://figma.redwood.internal/console/correlation-scout (wireframes + interaction flows). PRD for scope: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Console/Correlation+Scout. Example runtime event schema snippet and sample trace dataset stored in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/Shared/Tracing/CorrelationScout/samples.csv.

Open questions: - Should the Span Lens surface auto-generated root-cause tags (e.g., "KV eviction spike") or only surface raw telemetry? (ops vs trust tradeoff) - How granular should cost microbreakdowns be for privacy-sensitive customers? - Should playback animate KV cache sizes or keep it as a static histogram?
